item.title: Luck turns around for Golden Knights in shootout win over Jets
item.description: Nov 21, 2026; Winnipeg, Manitoba, CAN; Vegas Golden Knights center William Karlsson (71) score the winning goal in the shoot out on Winnipeg Jets goaltender Stuart Skinner (74) at Canada Life Centre. WINNIPEG—Heading back on the road, the Vegas Golden Knights needed any sort of momentum to get their season back on track. Sitting in second place in the Pacific Division by a comfortable margin, the Golden Knights were hardly in danger of losing their place in the standings. However, four straight losses to close out a five-game homestand undoubtedly left a sour taste in the mouths of players, coaches and fans alike. Between the loss to the last-place Vancouver Canucks, three losses last regulation and two straight third-period collapses against the Dallas Stars, the Golden Knights were in need of anything to stem the tide against them. Now on a road trip that will go beyond Thanksgiving, the Golden Knights finally got a break from their recent stretch of hard luck, securing a 5-4 shootout victory over the Winnipeg Jets to snap their losing streak. The Jets would force the Golden Knights on the back foot from the opening shot, as captain Adam Lowry would deflect Elias Salomonsson’s shot past Carter Hart to open the scoring in favor of the home side. However, the Golden Knights would come roaring back, starting with a clean faceoff win from Jack Eichel leading to a quick shot from Brett Howden that Winnipeg goaltender Stuart Skinner was unable to see. Less than 90 seconds later, Trevor Connelly and Mitch Marner continued to showcase their impressive chemistry, with the latter collecting a pass from the former and eventually potting in his own rebound for Vegas’ first lead of the night. The lead would not last through the end of the first period, as Eichel would cough up the puck in the neutral zone in the final minutes to lead to a tying goal from Jets rookie forward Viggo Bjorck. In the second period, controversy would strike during a Golden Knights power play when the net would come off its moorings before Tomas Hertl’s shot made it in. However, the referees would rule that Victor Olofsson was knocked into the net by Jets forward Alex Iafallo, counting the goal in favor of Vegas. The Winnipeg crowd’s vitriol would quickly turn into euphoria, as forward Mark Scheifele would pass Jets legend Dale Hawerchuk on the franchise’s all-time record with his 380th goal to tie the game at three. Kyle Connor would push the Jets back into the lead but, with less than four minutes remaining, a smart play from Hertl would give Ivan Barbashev time and space in the slot to sink a perfect shot past Skinner to push the Golden Knights to overtime for the third straight game. Despite some struggles, Hart would settle in with some key saves in the third period and overtime to preserve a point and keep the Golden Knights in it. item.description: Tornike Kvaratskhelia: Man United battling Arsenal, Chelsea for Georgian winger Manchester United’s pursuit of a talented young winger, who is fast earning admirers across the continent, is unlikely to be a walk in the park. The Red Devils were keen to bolster the left-forward role over the summer, but their failure to offload Marcus Rashford , who returned from a fruitful loan spell at Barcelona, perhaps hurt their plans. The Englishman has failed to replicate last season’s form and the Premier League giants have lacked threat on the wings. With Matheus Cunha hardly faring any better, there has been talk of further reinforcements for the position at the turn of the year. While United will be looking for an immediate fix for the position, they are also likely to have an eye out for the future. INEOS have targeted several talented young footballers since their arrival in 2024 to build a backbone for the future and it now appears that they have unearthed another gem, this time in Georgia. item.description: Lyndon Faulkner officially takes over as WRU chair in Decemeber [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Former Wales captain Jonathan Davies says new Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) chairman Lyndon Faulkner is the man to turn Welsh rugby around. The former Newport and Pontypool forward, who will take over from Richard Collier-Keywood , attends his first WRU annual general meeting (AGM) on Sunday. He has already promised to review everything including the controversial plan to cut a men's professional side by 2028, Faulkner has forged a highly successful business career in the United States of America. The 66-year-old also has a Welsh rugby background as the nephew of former Wales rugby prop Charlie Faulkner, who was yesterday inducted into World Rugby's hall of fame alongside Bobby Windsor and Graham Price - the famed Pontypool front-row. Former Wales fly-half Davies, who called for the WRU board to resign before Faulkner's appointment, believes the new will chair galvanise Welsh rugby off the field when he officially starts his role next month. “I believe the chair is a good guy and he has the opportunity to change things and he will make them,” said Davies. “He is a successful businessman, but he is a rugby man." Davies has described the problems at the WRU as similar to Manchester United. “When I look at Man United, I also look at the WRU," Davies told BBC 5 Live sport. "When Man United changed and brought the bankers in there was no football knowledge and the same has happened in Welsh rugby." The former Wales captain said decisions that have been made by the union have been purely financial, and not rugby ones. “Lyndon is the right man and will make the necessary changes in the WRU to give these guys a better platform," Davies added. “It’s not going to happen overnight and if we don‘t make these changes we will be in tier two for a long time.” WRU names businessman Faulkner as new chairman WRU is to blame for current mess - Davies Jonathan Davies is a former dual-code rugby international [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Davies believes the WRU needs to help the players who earlier this month inspired the nation with a first victory against New Zealand in 73 years, a match played in front of just over 55,000 fans. “I heard Dewi Lake say something before the New Zealand game and I felt really sorry for the players," said Davies. “He said because the attendance was low that was down to them. item.title: Five quick takeaways from Las Vegas GP
item.description: Motorsport photo Las Vegas gets the pack race it craved In America's artificial entertainment capital, F1 put the most artificial and entertaining spectacle. How fitting. The yo-yo racing from the early days of the 2026 season was back on full display, with the lack of electric energy available on the Strip's mile long straight bring back battery driven overtaking. For a while it felt like we were watching the Indy 500, with the top cars trading the lead without being able to break away from the rest of the pack. It led to numerous position changes and plenty of wheel-to-wheel races, much to the delight of the soldout crowd and event officials. It's certainly not for everyone, but you can't deny there was something to watch. And it was certainly a much better watch than the Madring's Spanish Grand Prix. - Fil Cleeren Ferrari in meltdown as Hamilton and Leclerc clash again Ferrari came into Las Vegas with two clear objectives: Try to win (naturally) and try to lockdown second place in the F1 world constructors’ championship. While the first target was going to be a tall order given the Scuderia’s lack of engine punch on the long Las Vegas straights, not losing more than 10 points to Red Bull was entirely realistic to second P2. But then the unsolved objectives reared up once again. Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc seem unable to race each other as team-mates. That much was evident in Mexico as they cost each other the win, but clear-the-air talks were meant to have solved all that in Brazil. Two weeks later, it is worse than ever. Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Hamilton vented his fury at Leclerc for fighting him in the pack during the opening act of the Las Vegas GP slipstreaming, battery-boosting ‘race’, with the Monegasque on the scene when he ran off the road and kept ahead of Lando Norris to pick up a 10-second penalty. After having to serve his penalty a lap into the safety car period, in order not to hold up Leclerc who was behind him, the pair re-engaged their on-track disagreements and it was Leclerc’s turn to make the error. But this time he clattered into his team-mate, spinning Hamilton around, and earning himself a 10s penalty. item.title: F1 Las Vegas GP: Max Verstappen wins thriller as Ferraris come to blows
item.description: Motorsport photo Max Verstappen won an eventful Las Vegas Grand Prix, holding off both Mercedes as Formula 1’s novel ‘yo-yo’ racing returned – with no Silver Arrow on the eventual podium. With qualifying pacesetter Kimi Antonelli taking a five-place grid penalty for exceeding his engine allocation, Max Verstappen inherited pole position and retained the lead from George Russell at the start with an unchanged top five: Lando Norris, Isack Hadjar and Arvid Lindblad followed – though Hadjar swiftly found a way past the McLaren on lap one. The only top-10 driver starting on mediums, Antonelli lost two spots to the Alpines at lights out, finding himself eighth ahead of the Ferraris, who were out in Q2 – though Franco Colapinto would soon collapse from seventh to 10th, then out of the points-paying positions. Verstappen couldn’t break away from Russell, and the Briton briefly snatched the lead away on lap two before the Dutchman immediately responded. Russell couldn’t attack the leader again and was instead overtaken by the sister Red Bull car. Now it was these two trading places… until Lindblad remarkably overtook Norris and Russell in quick succession, even though he could not hold the Mercedes off. Meanwhile, Hadjar was pressuring Verstappen for the lead but had to deal with Russell’s attacks. “We need to not lose time as a team,” the Frenchman was told. “Can he stop defending?” he inquired about his team-mate’s driving. Hadjar briefly took the lead soon after, though he dropped to third moments later. On lap 10, the top 10 cars still lay within four seconds. Russell momentarily retook the lead (again) as Pierre Gasly fought to third, though he couldn’t hold off Hadjar for long. There were no changes among the top four for a moment, but Norris’ collapse continued as he ended up outside the top 10. Russell took the lead back on laps 14 and 18, but this was again Turn 14 moves with Verstappen sweeping back past on the start/finish straight. The second time, Hadjar snuck by in second. Meanwhile, the Ferraris were battling both their rivals and among themselves for seventh place. Charles Leclerc called on his team-mate to “be careful with this squeezing”; Lewis Hamilton said the sister car should “back the f**k off” – and copped a 10-second penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage. (AP) — Kate Harpring scored 20 points, Achol Akot added 16 and No. 24 North Carolina used two runs in the second half on Saturday to defeat Alabama 78-64 at the WBCA Showcase. The 16th and final lead change came during a 13-0 run to end the third quarter. Harping hit a pair of 3s and a 3 from Laila Hull at the buzzer gave the Tar Heels a 60-50 lead. Hull hit another 3 after the Crimson Tide got with seven points midway through the fourth quarter, starting a 10-0 run capped by a 3-pointer from Nyla Brooks that made it 76-59 with less than 2 minutes to go. Brooks added 14 points for the Tar Heels (4-2), who went 12 of 28 from the 3-point line and shot 46% overall to overcome a 4 of 11 showing at the foul line. Ace Austin had 15 points for the Crimson Tide (6-2). Alayna West added 13 points off the bench and Aaliyah Roberson scored 11. The Tar Heels scored the first nine points of the game but the Crimson Tide scrapped back to lead 38-36 at the half. Alabama had three turnovers and missed two shots but then made five straight to get back in the game and there were 11 lead changes before the break. item.description: Chelsea FC v Leeds United - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Dominic Calvert-Lewin urged his Leeds United team-mates to savour their first Stamford Bridge triumph since 1999 after dismantling Chelsea 4-1 in the Premier League. The in-form striker converted a crucial second-half penalty and insisted Xabi Alonso's hosts simply could not handle Leeds' relentless intensity. Calvert-Lewin relishes long-awaited Bridge triumph Dominic Calvert-Lewin called on Leeds United to savour their 4-1 Premier League demolition of Chelsea after helping the Whites secure their first victory at Stamford Bridge since 1999. The striker rattled home a pivotal second-half penalty between Noah Okafor's brace before substitute Brenden Aaronson added a stoppage-time fourth. Celebrations erupted inside the away end and visiting dressing room as Leeds climbed up to sixth in the table . "Great feeling," Calvert-Lewin said. "I think you can see it at the end, the way we celebrated it. It's always great to win in the Premier League, especially away from home in a place like Stamford Bridge, so I think you have to enjoy it." Relentless intensity overwhelms Alonso's Chelsea Leeds fell behind midway through the first half when Emmanuel Emegha fired Chelsea ahead on his full debut, only for Okafor to equalise within three minutes. Rather than fading after the interval, Daniel Farke's men stepped up their pressing, won a penalty when a shot struck Morgan Rogers high on the arm, and blew the Blues away. "We expected them to probably come out with a bit more of a reaction, and we started the second half exactly the same as we started the first, which was intensity," Calvert-Lewin explained. Peak fitness fuels striker's confident streak Calvert-Lewin proved a constant aerial menace throughout the contest, rattling Emiliano Martinez's crossbar with an early header before dispatching his spot-kick into the bottom corner. Fresh from winning in Madrid with England during the international break, the forward credited his physical rhythm for his commanding display. "I'm feeling comfortable in my body at the moment and really enjoying my football," Calvert-Lewin revealed. "And for me, when I feel like that, going onto a football pitch, I feel like I can play against anybody, so I'm full of confidence at the moment. A great seven days and a great result coming back in." Momentum builds for top-six contenders The victory capped an unforgettable week for Calvert-Lewin and underlined Leeds' growing credentials under Farke as they moved into sixth place ahead of the weekend's remaining fixtures. With Okafor clinical in front of goal and the squad brimming with belief, Leeds carry formidable momentum into the busy winter schedule. item.description: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images Spurs star Victor Wembanyama drops tough ‘stat padding’ declaration after dropping 50 on Pelicans appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Victor Wembanyama put together one of the most dominant performances of the NBA season on Saturday night , but the San Antonio Spurs star refused to take himself too seriously afterward. Wembanyama erupted for 50 points, 19 rebounds, five blocks and four steals as the Spurs cruised to a 114-91 victory over the New Orleans Pelicans at Frost Bank Center. When asked during his postgame interview how special it was to reach such a rare threshold, the 22-year-old offered a playful jab at the rest of the league. “It is very special. But unlike many of my peers, I’m not very good at stat-padding. So, I haven’t reached it yet,” Wembanyama said, via the Spurs X account. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) "Unlike many of my peers, i'm not very good at statpadding" Victor Wembanyama after his 50-point outburst 😳 (via @spurs ) pic.twitter.com/kdNFR3BpYR — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 22, 2026 The comment was classic Wembanyama, whose dry sense of humor has become a regular part of his postgame routine. He finished just one rebound shy of a 50-point, 20-rebound night. There was nothing padded about his numbers, though. Wembanyama shot an efficient 20-of-29 from the field, including 5-of-11 from beyond the arc, and San Antonio outscored New Orleans by 35 points with him on the floor. The Spurs led by as many as 29 points. The outing also cemented his place in the history books . Wembanyama became just the fourth player in NBA history with at least 50 points, 15 rebounds and five blocks in a game, joining Wilt Chamberlain, Anthony Davis and Bob McAdoo. He has now done it twice this month, after putting up 52 points, 24 rebounds and eight blocks against the Dallas Mavericks on Nov. 4. Wembanyama also joined David Robinson as the only players to record multiple 50-point, five-block games since blocks became an official stat in 1973-74. Stephon Castle added 19 points and hit five 3-pointers for the Spurs, while De’Aaron Fox dished out 10 assists. Jeremiah Fears paced the Pelicans with 29 points, and Jordan Poole scored 25. San Antonio improved to 14-3 with the victory and has won 12 of its last 13 games . If this is what Wembanyama looks like when he isn’t chasing numbers, the rest of the league should be worried about what happens when he actually tries. As a result, he is expected to be out for four to five months, thus ruling him out for the remainder of the regular season, and possibly any playoff run the Rams make. Fans had drastically different reactions to the news of Nacua’s injury, with some criticising his recent trouble with the NFL, while others criticised Sean McVay for keeping Nacua in a game longer than needed, thus leading to his injury. One fan wrote: “Last snap as a Ram has been played. item.title: Ospreys legends set to turn out to honour Tipuric
item.description: Justin Tipuric gave up the Ospreys captaincy in 2024 with Jac Morgan taking over [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Welsh rugby fans will have a chance to pay tribute to Ospreys and Wales legend Justin Tipuric at St Helen's in Swansea on Sunday (14:30 GMT). An Ospreys legends vs Trebanos XV event will see Tipuric's only professional side take on his village club. The Ospreys legends squad includes former flanker Tipuric joined by fellow ex-Wales internationals Alun Wyn Jones, Shane Williams, James Hook, Richard Hibbard, Ian Gough, Scott Baldwin, Duncan Jones and Huw Bennett, while former back-rower and current Dragons head coach Filo Tiatia has also signed up. While Tipuric has been named in the Ospreys squad, he is expected to play for both sides. Tipuric lines ups among Ospreys legends Alun Wyn Jones and Justin Tipuric both retired from international rugby on the same day before the 2023 World Cup [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Tipuric retired at the end of the 2024-25 season to become Ospreys' defence coach. He was due to have a farewell home match at the old Swansea.com Stadium ground against Dragons in May 2025, but missed the match after picking up a pectoral injury against Lyon earlier that month. "There was a bit of a stick from a couple of the Trebanos guys saying they came down with a lot of the juniors to watch, but I wasn't even playing," said Tipuric. Ospreys have organised this occasion so fans can see Tipuric's famous blue scrum cap one more time on the rugby field. "The Ospreys said once we have our stadium done at St Helen's they wanted to make sure I had a game," added Tipuric. "Until I saw us kick off at St Helen's I didn't think I would see that happen because for the 20 years I've been involved, I've seen about five or six different plans. "I thought they had forgotten about it, so I didn't have to play, but they have been amazing with Richard Lancaster [Ospreys managing director] and so many people working behind the scenes." Shane Williams scored 58 tries in 87 internationals for Wales [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Modest man insists event is not about him The event does not have the Tipuric name in the title because the player himself was not keen on the spotlight. His insistence this is not labelled a testimonial match or a celebration of his career underlines how humble the flanker was during his playing days. Tipuric was always happier speaking about others than himself. His modesty off the field was matched by his brilliance on it. "It is definitely not about me, this is something for Ospreys, Trebanos and the fans," said Tipuric. "There are matches for the Trebanos juniors starting at 9am so they can get to play on the St Helen's pitch. "For the match itself, it will just be great to get people back in the building who have put an Ospreys jersey on during the last 20 years. "It's something we've never done before so that is quite special especially, hopefully, for the Ospreys fans, who have been amazing to me throughout my career."

item.title: Islanders 3, Red Wings 2: Palat pair overcomes post luck
item.description: A thousand games and a thousand hugs. | NHLI via Getty Images The Islanders banked another two points against an opponent they should beat, riding Ondrej Palat’s two goals to a 3-2 over the Red Wings in Detroit. Despite a good effort — certainly better than a couple nights ago in Winnipeg — it looked like things might not go their way when they were hitting posts (including Mathew Barzal, twice) while the Red Wings held a 1-0 lead thanks to a fortunate Joe Louis Little Caesar’s Whatever Arena end boards. But Palat scored midway through the second to tie it at 1-1, Simon Holmstrom finished off a broken 4-on-2 early i the third to give them the lead, and Ilya Sorokin made a sterling save to preserve the lead shortly before Palat extended it to 3-1. Alex DeBrincat, who is toiling away to honor his commitment to the Red Wings’ perpetual rebuild, scored his eighth of the season to make it close again with under seven minutes to go. Holmstrom’s goal, by the way, was his tenth. [ NHL Gamecenter | Game Summary | Event Summary | Natural Stat Trick ] It was a satisfying outcome for Casey Cizikas’ 1,000th regular season NHL game, complete with two goals from his fourth-line mate Palat. The 1,000 gamer also had a big shot block on Moritz Seider as time wound down to help seal the win. In addition to making a suite available for his family and friends who were in attendance, the Red Wings also gave him a Jumbotron salute during a TV stoppage. That drew a visit and embrace from Ben Chiarot, who fought Brayden Schenn a period later after the Wings defenseman roughed up Matthew Schaefer. (And that came after Chiarot got a roughing penalty for doing similar to Victor Eklund earlier in the period.) With the win, the Islanders keep pace in the wild card hunt, two points (27) behind current holders Florida (29), and with two games in hand. Up Next The Islanders return home to host the Leafs on Monday, the Blues on Wednesday and the Jets on Friday. Until then, find yourself someone who hugs you like Casey Cizikas hugs his victorious goalies.

item.description: SIOUX FALLS, S.D. (SKYFORCE) --- The Sioux Falls Skyforce (6-0) erased a 16-point deficit and used a 43-point fourth quarter to defeat the Windy City Bulls (4-3) 128-119 on Saturday night in front of 2,683 fans at the Sanford Pentagon, completing a two-game weekend sweep. Miami HEAT two-way center Vladislav Goldin led Sioux Falls with 31 points on 12-14 shooting from the field, tying his season high while adding eight rebounds and three blocks. item.description: Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images Luka Doncic has urged Austin Reaves to take his time recovering from a heel injury after revealing how a similar problem once affected his own career. The Los Angeles Lakers are waiting for Reaves to return from a left heel bruise, with the guard currently being monitored on a day-to-day basis. Doncic has experienced the same issue before and is keen to ensure his teammate does not make the mistake of rushing back too soon. Luka Doncic warns Austin Reaves after previous heel injury setback According to ESPN’s Dave McMenamin , Doncic personally shared his experience with Reaves and explained why he should prioritise his long-term fitness. A source close to the Lakers star revealed the message Doncic delivered: “I’ve dealt with a bruised heel back in 2024, and it led to a calf strain, which ultimately led to me being traded from the Dallas Mavericks to the Lakers. We don’t want you to be in a similar situation. We’re trying to be in this for the long haul. Take your time now – we’re 13-3, and we’ll hold down the fort.” Doncic’s warning comes from personal experience, having seen his heel problem develop into a calf strain before his eventual move from Dallas to Los Angeles. Meanwhile, Reaves’ recovery has reportedly been progressing positively. McMenamin revealed that the guard had returned to the court for a workout, although the Lakers were prepared to remain cautious with his comeback. He added that Reaves had been improving day by day and that the team recognised the value of giving him additional rest before its next game. Quentin Grimes has stepped up in Reaves’ absence, but the Lakers have had some uncomfortable moments without one of their key offensive options. They suffered an upset defeat to Utah and were pushed hard by Charlotte and Sacramento before securing narrow victories. Los Angeles did manage to beat the Kings 106-104, with Doncic recording 25 points, eight assists and four rebounds. With the Lakers sitting at 14-3, Doncic clearly believes there is no reason to risk Reaves’ fitness for an immediate return. The priority is having him available for the longer campaign. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. Efforts to build a complex in Baltimore for an MLS Next Pro operation have floundered. (Meanwhile, United's owners have launched a pro volleyball team.)
